title.value: Uncertainty Evaluation Metric for Brain Tumour Segmentation
title.justification: The paper focuses on developing a metric designed to assess and rank uncertainty measures specifically for brain tumour segmentation.
title.quote: In this paper, we develop a metric designed to assess and rank uncertainty measures for the task of brain tumour sub-tissue segmentation.

analysis.description: The paper proposes a new metric for evaluating uncertainty measures in brain tumour segmentation tasks. It focuses on rewarding high confidence in correct predictions and penalizing high confidence in incorrect predictions. The evaluation was conducted using data from the BraTS 2019 challenge.

type.justification: The study involves the application and assessment of different uncertainty metrics on data, indicating empirical research through experimentation and observation.
type.quote: These metrics were combined and used as the basis of ranking the uncertainties produced by participating teams in the BraTS 2019 sub-challenge on uncertainty quantification.

name.justification: The research is conducted in the context of brain tumour segmentation in medical images, which is a subfield of Medical Imaging.
name.quote: Including tumour segmentation, as depicted by the highest ranking results on recent BraTS challenges.

name.justification: The paper focuses on segmentation of brain tumour tissues, which is explicitly stated as the task.
name.quote: For the task of brain tumour sub-tissue segmentation in the BraTS 2019 sub-challenge on uncertainty quantification.

name.justification: The study is centered around different uncertainty measures and their evaluation.
name.quote: Several recent methods have been proposed to estimate uncertainties in deep neural networks.

name.justification: The paper uses a modified 3D U-Net architecture to generate segmentation outputs.
name.quote: A modified 3D U-Net architecture (Çiçek et al., 2016; Mehta and Arbel, 2018) generates the segmentation outputs and corresponding uncertainties.

is_contributed.justification: The paper uses an existing architecture (3D U-Net), which is not introduced as a novel contribution.
is_contributed.quote: A modified 3D U-Net architecture (Çiçek et al., 2016; Mehta and Arbel, 2018) generates the segmentation outputs and corresponding uncertainties.

is_executed.justification: The model was trained, validated, and tested during the study.
is_executed.quote: We train (228), validate (57), and test (50) this network based on the publicly available Brain Tumour Segmentation (BraTS) challenge 2019 training dataset.

is_compared.justification: The paper does not mention a direct numerical comparison to other models; it focuses on evaluating uncertainty measures.
is_compared.quote: The study focuses on evaluating uncertainty measures rather than comparing different models numerically.
